gybe: To shift a fore-and-aft sail from one side of a sailing vessel to the other, while sailing before the wind.
gybed: simple past and past participle of gybe
gybing: present participle and gerund of gybe
gym: Clipping of gymnasium; especially, a school gymnasium.
gymkhana: A competition where riders and horses display a range of skills and aptitudes.
gymnasium: A large room or building for indoor sports.
gymnast: One who performs (the sport of) gymnastics.
gymnastics: A sport involving the performance of sequences of movements requiring physical strength, flexibility, and kinesthetic awareness.
gymnosophist: One of a school of ancient Indian ascetic philosophers, reported in antiquity, who wore little clothing; a mystic.
gymnosperm: Any plant such as a conifer whose seeds are not enclosed in an ovary.
gymnospermous: Having seeds that are not protected in a capsule
gynaeceum: The women's quarters in a household; (hence, loosely) any building or area for women.
gynandromorph: An insect, crustacean or bird literally having physical characteristics of both sexes, usually displaying a bilateral difference.
gynandromorphism: The condition of being a gynandromorph.
gynandrous: Having stamens and pistils together in a column.
gynandry: Hermaphroditism, intersexuality; androgyny; resemblance (by a member of one sex) of another sex.
gynarchy: A government ruled by a woman or women.
gynecocracy: Government or rule by women, or a society with such leadership.
gynecologist: A physician specializing in diseases of the female reproductive system.
gynecology: The study of, or the branch of medicine specializing in, the medical problems of women, especially disorders of the reproductive organs.
gynecomastia: Excessive development of breasts in men, resembling the breast development in women.
gyniatry: The study of women's diseases; gynecology.
gynoecium: The pistils/carpels of a flower considered as a group
gynogenesis: Female parthenogenesis in which the embryo contains only maternal chromosomes due to the failure of the sperm to fuse with the egg nucleus.
gynophore: The stalk of a pistil; the stalk, present in certain flowers (such as those of the genera Telopea and Brachychiton), which supports the gynoecium.
gyp: A cheat or swindle; a rip-off.
gyplure: A potent gypsy moth attractant synthesized from ricinoleic acid.
gypped: simple past and past participle of gyp
gypper: One who gyps; a cheat or swindler.
gypping: present participle and gerund of gyp
gypsied: simple past and past participle of gypsy
gypsophila: Any of the many flowering plants of the genus Gypsophila, which have a profusion of small pink or white flowers.
gypsum: A mineral consisting of hydrated calcium sulphate.
gypsy: An itinerant person or any person, not necessarily Romani; a tinker, a traveller or a carny.
gypsydom: The realm or sphere of gypsies.
gypsying: present participle and gerund of gypsy
gypsyism: The state of being a gypsy.
gyral: Of or pertaining to a gyrus
gyrate: To revolve round a central point; to move spirally about an axis, as a tornado.
gyrated: simple past and past participle of gyrate
gyrates: third-person singular simple present indicative of gyrate
gyrating: present participle and gerund of gyrate
gyration: The act of turning or whirling, especially around a fixed axis or centre; a circular or spiral motion; rotation.
gyrational: Of, pertaining to, or caused by gyration
gyratory: Moving in a circle, or spirally; revolving; whirling around.
gyred: simple past and past participle of gyre
gyrene: A member of the United States Marine Corps.
gyrfalcon: Any large falcon, especially as used to fly at herons.
gyring: present participle and gerund of gyre
gyrocompass: A north-seeking form of gyroscope used as a directional reference in navigation.
gyrofrequency: The frequency of the circular motion of a charged particle in the presence of a uniform magnetic field.
gyromagnetic: of, relating to, or resulting from the properties of a spinning magnet, or a spinning electric charge; magnetogyric
gyron: A triangular form having an angle at the fess point and the opposite side at the edge of the escutcheon.
gyroplane: Any aircraft that obtains lift from both rotating blades and small wings.
gyroscope: An apparatus composed of a wheel which spins inside of a frame (gimbal) and causes the balancing of the frame in any direction or position.
gyroscopic: Pertaining to, by means of, or in the manner of a gyroscope.
gyrose: Turned round like a crook, or bent to and fro.
gyrostabilizer: A device for stabilizing using a gyroscope.
gyrostat: A gyroscope fixed within a rigid case.
gyrus: A fold or ridge on the cerebral cortex of the brain.
gyve: A shackle or fetter, especially for the leg.
gyved: simple past and past participle of gyve
gyving: present participle and gerund of gyve
